newsitem.title: MEXICO: Clarke says Britain to spur trade with Mexico.
newsitem.headline: Clarke says Britain to spur trade with Mexico.

text.p: Britain's Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke, hailing Mexico's recovery from crisis, said his country would slice rates on export credit guarantees to spur trade between the two countries.

"We've decided that the performance of the last two years justifies a very big reappraisal of risk...so we are about to start reducing export credit guarantee premiums, in some cases by up to 50 percent," he told a news conference on Monday at the end of a week-long visit to Mexico.

He was unable to put a figure on the credit guarantee rates but said the cuts would encourage British businessmen to trade with Mexico after several years of stalling before and after Mexico's devastating 1994 peso crash.

British exports to Mexico grew eight percent in 1996, he said, and the country remains the second-biggest overseas investor in Mexico after the United States with a $4 billion portfolio. Bilateral trade between the two countries is about $1 billion per year.
Clarke played down the impact on trade and investment of Mexico's critical mid-term Congressional elections on July 7.

Some pollsters and political analysts expect President Ernesto Zedillo's Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) to lose its majority in the Chamber of Deputies for the first time in nearly 68 years of power.
Clarke said most foreign investors believed Zedillo's policy of pursuing sound public finances and low inflation would not "be shaken off course" by the elections, no matter who wins.

Referring to Britain, which also has to call a general election by mid-May which the opposition Labour Party is tipped to win, he stressed that monetary policy would continue to be geared toward achieving 2.5 percent inflation.
He declined to say whether brisk Christmas retail sales in Britain would force him to push up interest rates before the elections.
